comments.author: PythagoRascal
comments.story: Tiny Glade 'built' its way to >600k sold in a month
comments.why: Detailed talk on the tile-adjacency wave-function-collapse technique behind Bad North.
comments.text: As far as I know they are using a customised variant of the "wave-function collapse" technique, used and popularised by Oskar Stalberg in his games "Bad North" and "Townscaper". The technique boils down to hand-crafting tons of tiles with adjacency rules about which tiles can slot together. When the user adds/removes a tile the algorithm iteratively tries to find fitting tiles and, if needed, changes neighbouring tiles for ones with the best transitions. He gave a talk where he goes into detail about this[1]. You can also find more if you google his name and "wave-function collapse". [1]: [VIDEO]

comments.author: hesdeadjim
comments.story: WaveFunctionCollapse: Generates bitmaps that are locally similar to the input
comments.why: Shows Wave Function Collapse used in the game Bad North.
comments.text: I played around a lot with this library: [LINK] Fun stuff, but I struggled to get a lot of value out of using it for level gen. You get cool patterns, but levels need structure and intent to be interesting. Adding constraints to the algorithm becomes a big-oh nightmare and you end up with frequently unsolvable paths as the algorithm recurses. The game Bad North used it to good effect, so depending on the game it may be a very useful tool in the toolbelt. [VIDEO]
